description: Describe one treatment line: water flow, chlorine dosing pump, contact tank and two virtual chlorine sensors.
Agree the teaching assumptions, units and response delays; label values as simulation settings rather than real treatment limits.
Write small stories for normal operation, an approved change, an unapproved change, equipment failure and unreliable sensor readings.
Define the expected behaviour and evidence for each story before implementation.
actual_result: Eleven check definitions and planned evidence packages prepared; criteria/named agreement pending; all runtime results Not run.
blocker: Awaiting review capacity: 4 Review cards at preparation versus limit 3; DOS-1/DOS-2/DOS-3 inputs pending.
next_action: Keep In Progress; move to Review only when fewer than 3 cards already occupy Review. Record all six interface findings and Donald acceptance; do not imply runtime passes.

description: Install the open-source version of FUXA and Python with PyModbus on the development laptop; record the versions used.
Install the FUXA Modbus driver through Plugins and configure a local connection to the virtual device.
Configure one test reading in PyModbus and bind it to a numeric display in FUXA; verify the address, units and scaling.
Save the configuration and prove that the reading still appears after stopping and restarting both applications.
Represent water flow and chlorine feed using a small Python model with clearly documented inputs and outputs.
Calculate a simplified chlorine residual after mixing and delay in the contact tank; use a documented chlorine-demand assumption.
Keep the requested pump setting separate from actual simulated delivery so a running command can still produce poor or zero delivery.
Add initial values, start/pause/reset controls and saved scenario settings; fix random seeds when noise is used.
Define a Modbus register map for requested dose, accepted setting, pump state, water flow and actual delivery, including units and writable fields.
Use the PyModbus server as the virtual device interface and connect it to the plant model; implement the small control behaviour required.
Return command acknowledgement separately from equipment feedback; record whether a setting was accepted and what the pump actually delivered.
Add no-flow behaviour and selectable faults for an ignored command, a stopped pump and reduced delivery.
Create a small authenticated interface for named operators to request a dose change; record change ID, equipment, chemical, target and time.
Allow a different named user to approve a request; record the approver, approved value or range, expiry and approval time.
Execute approved requests through the virtual controller; retain the request, approval, command and acknowledgement with the same change ID.
Add an explicitly labelled lab-only unapproved-change scenario that retains the actor and command records for DoseProof to assess later.
Create sensors A and B that sample the modeled water state instead of copying the controller setpoint or FUXA display.
Give each sensor its own source ID, sequence number, timestamp, reading, units and quality indication; configure separate noise seeds.
Add selectable missing, delayed, stuck and biased readings; allow one sensor to disagree with the other.
Test each sensor fault separately and document that both sensors share a software model and laptop, so independence is limited.
Use the FUXA editor to create a simple screen showing the water inlet, dosing pump, contact tank and sensors with clear labels.
Bind the equipment symbols and displays to virtual readings; verify pump state, flow, requested setting, actual delivery and chlorine units.
Add sensor trends and connection or stale-data indications; show unavailable values clearly instead of treating them as zero.
Keep dose execution in the request/approval desk; configure this FUXA view for reading and remove dose-write controls.
Agree the event fields with element 2: run ID, event ID, change ID where applicable, source ID, sequence, timestamps, units and quality.
Produce local sample records for requests, approvals, commands, acknowledgements, equipment feedback and each sensor source.
Preserve source timestamps and identities; mark missing or unknown information explicitly instead of inventing values.
Save examples for normal and fault scenarios and document their meaning; leave transport, collection and validation to elements 2 and 3.
Run a normal baseline and an approved dose change; check the command trail, actual delivery and delayed sensor response against the story expectations.
Run the unapproved-change, equipment-fault and sensor-fault stories; retain the source records and screenshots that demonstrate each condition.
Verify that the plant can run without DoseProof connected and continues when its monitoring stops; reset and rerun the demonstration.
Write a short startup/reset guide, save the FUXA configuration and scenario files, demonstrate the increment and turn feedback into backlog corrections.
